fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into an Alumni Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the table behind it, and one more prompt changes either before the next class graduates.
fields.feature_1:
Sections for what your office needs

Tell Emergent what you need to learn, such as career paths, reunion plans, or mentoring interest. It drafts a section for each, and a short prompt changes any question.
fields.feature_2:
Answers sorted by class year

Each response lands as a row in a database you own, tagged with class year and degree. Put the class of 2025 beside the class of 2026 on the same question, line by line.
fields.feature_3:
Matched to your alumni records

The app connects to the records system your office keeps through its API, so answers sync in and new contact details sync out. Nobody has to retype a graduate's new job title.
fields.feature_4:
An email when an answer needs a reply

Set a rule on any answer, such as a graduate still job hunting. The app sends an email or Slack alert to the staff member who follows up, with the full answer attached.
fields.feature_5:
Built for a phone, with no response cap

Alumni answer one question per screen on a phone, between other things. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so a class of 40 and an alumni base of 40,000 use one survey.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Host the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it for next year's class.

fields.usecase_heading: How Schools and Firms Run Alumni Surveys
fields.tab_content_1:
118 of 151 graduates who answered are working

Quarrybank College's engineering school surveys all 212 graduates 6 months after commencement. Of the 212, 151 answer: 118 are working, 22 are in graduate school, and 11 are still looking. Each of the 11 gets an email inviting them to book a session with the career center.
fields.tab_content_2:
Reunion vote goes to homecoming, 104 to 61

Brierwood High School's class of 2016 asks 340 classmates to pick its 10-year reunion weekend, one vote per classmate, checked against the class list. Of the 340, 196 vote. Homecoming weekend gets 104 votes, the Friday after Thanksgiving gets 61, and the July 4 weekend gets 31. The committee books homecoming.
fields.tab_content_3:
Health care asks for 38 mentors and gets 6

Merrivale University's alumni office wanted a mentor for every student who asked. It asked graduates if they would mentor, and in what field: 74 alumni signed up against 98 student requests. Finance has 31 mentors for 22 requests. Health care has 6 mentors for 38 requests. The office writes to its nursing alumni first.
fields.tab_content_4:
A recruiter email for every former consultant who says yes

Thornquist Advisory keeps in touch with 412 former employees through a spring survey answered on a phone, one question per screen. This year 187 answered, and 23 said they would consider coming back. For each yes, recruiter Marisol Raske gets an email with the person's name and last role.

fields.howto_title: How to Run an Alumni Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to run an alumni survey that reaches your graduates and ends with one decision your office acts on.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the decision this round settles
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about today before the past
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tag answers by class and degree
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the results will change before you write anything: next year's career programs, a reunion date, or a mentor recruiting push. One decision per round keeps the survey short. Put it in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Remove addresses that bounced on the last mailing, add the personal emails collected at commencement, and tag every contact with class year and degree. A survey reaches only the graduates your list can find.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Open with what graduates do now: employer, job title, city, or further study. Put questions about their program after that, while they are still engaged. Keep the whole survey near 12 questions. A graduate should be able to finish it on a phone in one sitting.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for class year and degree, or fill them in from the contact list. Every answer can then be split by school and year. A nursing result and a business result blended into one average tell neither school what to change.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Test it with three recent graduates
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to three recent graduates and ask them to answer with real details. Check that each answer lands in the right column and that any alert rule fires on the right answer. Fix every question one of them misread.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it from a name they know
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the invite from a professor or the class president rather than a no-reply inbox. Leave the survey open for 3 weeks with 2 reminders, and stop the reminders for anyone who has already answered.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Report back and repeat next year
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tell respondents what changed because of their answers: the reunion date, the new mentor push, the career sessions added. Keep the core questions the same next year. Each class then compares with the one before it.

faq_plan.a: It is a questionnaire for the former students of a school, asking what they do now and how they see the place they left. A school can use one to count career outcomes or recruit mentors, and a firm can send the same kind of survey to former employees it may rehire.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an alumni survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: who receives it, what you need to learn, and what should happen to each answer. Emergent builds the survey, the database behind it, and a results dashboard, and a follow-up prompt changes any part. Send it to a few recent graduates as a test before the full list.

faq_plan.q: Which alumni survey questions give a career office data it can count?
faq_plan.a: Questions with fixed answers: current status (working, in graduate school, or still looking), employer and job title, and how closely the job relates to the degree. Add one open question, such as what the program should have taught them. Cut any question that no one in your office will act on.

faq_plan.q: What should an alumni survey template include?
faq_plan.a: It should hold the parts every round repeats: class year and degree, current status, updated contact details, one section for this round's decision, and a closing comment box. Keep the career section plain. If the survey also warms people up for a reunion, put the funny survey questions in a separate event poll.

faq_plan.q: What are some alumni survey examples besides career outcomes?
faq_plan.a: Reunion date votes and mentor sign-ups are alumni surveys too, and so is a firm's yearly check-in with former staff. Each asks fewer questions than an outcomes survey and ends in one decision, such as a date or a list of names to contact.

faq_plan.q: How do I send an alumni survey to graduates with out-of-date email addresses?
faq_plan.hint: How schools automate alumni survey distribution?
faq_plan.a: Start with the addresses that still work, and make updated contact details the first screen of the survey. Collect personal emails before commencement, and post the link where graduates already gather, such as a class group or the alumni newsletter. The app Emergent builds can connect to your records system's API and sync the new details back.

faq_plan.q: Why do colleges run alumni surveys?
faq_plan.a: Colleges run them to learn what graduates do after they leave and how well the program prepared them. For first-destination reporting, NACE recommends as high a knowledge rate as possible: the percentage of the graduating class for whom an outcomes destination is known. For graduates who skip long forms, send a short yes no questions survey first.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an alumni survey have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for about 12 questions. A reunion vote needs only 3 or 4. Give every extra question a decision behind it. Built on Emergent, the survey can show one question per screen.

faq_plan.q: Should an alumni survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Not for career outcomes or mentoring, where a name is needed to update a record or make a match. For questions about how the program treated them, add an anonymous section that saves answers without a name, and say so in the invite. Every answer sits in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How often should I survey alumni?
faq_plan.a: Run a full survey once a year, in the same month each time, and add the 6-month outcome survey for the newest class. Between rounds, put a couple of poll questions in the alumni newsletter to keep in touch without another long survey.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook (Wave 3); university career offices own the SERP with their own outcome reports, and template pages list alumni questions and stop. This page shows four alumni surveys built from a prompt, each ending in a decision an alumni or career office makes: an engineering school's 6-month career outcomes count, a high school class voting on its 10-year reunion weekend, a university finding the field where mentor volunteers fall short of student requests, and a consulting firm's former-staff survey that emails its recruiter when someone is open to returning. Giving and course feedback stay with the donor and course evaluation pages; the FAQ covers questions, templates, examples, out-of-date contact lists, length, anonymity and cadence as plain advice.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Alumni Survey for Schools and Alumni Networks'; hero 'Get an alumni survey that tracks graduate outcomes and reunion plans, with every answer saved in a database you own.' (116 chars); how-to description one sentence.

intent.evidence: Four worked examples (career outcomes, reunion vote, mentor sign-up, former staff), template contents in FAQ 4, question types in FAQ 3 and how-to step 3, seven run steps, comparison table.

specificity.evidence: Alumni-office vocabulary throughout: 'tagged with class year and degree', 'personal emails collected at commencement', 'first-destination reporting'. Table generated from the library (QC V2/V3 pass).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Tell Emergent what you need to learn', 'Quarrybank College's engineering school surveys all 212 graduates', 'Remove addresses that bounced on the last mailing'.

craft.evidence: QC Q5 at 2 ', so' endings (under the block); sentences short and single-idea; tab 3 tense shift recorded as a note.

voice.evidence: Product-led and concrete: 'Each of the 11 gets an email inviting them to book a session with the career center.' Two forced sibling links recorded as a note.

truth.evidence: usecase_heading 'How Four Alumni Offices Use Their Surveys' is contradicted by three tabs: tab 1 is Quarrybank's engineering school and career center, tab 2 is Brierwood High's class of 2016 reunion committee ('The committee books homecoming'), tab 4 is Thornquist Advisory's recruiter. Only tab 3 is an alumni office. NACE knowledge-rate claim in FAQ 7 matches the Quinnipiac span; Emergent claims all map to claims_used.

distinct.evidence: No giving or course-feedback content (donor-survey, course-evaluation-survey own those); no school-climate content; QC D2 highest overlap 20% with board-survey hero (template slot).

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, paa --spec 10 pass / 0 reject / 0 flag; hub link in item 2; three sibling links (funny-survey-questions, yes-no-questions-survey, poll-questions); moat lines in items 6, 8, 9.

images.evidence: Contact sheet: each tab matches its copy on names and numbers (151 of 212; 104/61/31 of 196; 6 mentors for 38 requests; 23 of 187 to Marisol Raske); one hero per tab; cover 78% = 118/151.
